item.title: Nasinu claims Marama Championship thrashing Namosi 62-24
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 31/10/2026 The Nasinu Women's Rugby team has claimed the Subrails Marama Championship title after demolishing last year's champions, Namosi, 62-24 at Churchill Park in Lautoka.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 31/10/2026

The Nasinu Women's Rugby team has claimed the Subrails Marama Championship title after demolishing last year's champions, Namosi, 62-24 at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

Nasinu got off to a strong start, leading the defending champions 29-17 at halftime.

Namosi gathered their rhythm in the second half, but it was not enough to slow down Nasinu's momentum.

Meanwhile, Nadroga has won the U20 title after edging Nadi 41-39.

The Skipper Cup final match between Nadroga and Nadi is scheduled to kick off at 3pm today.

item.title: Discipline will be key to winning Skipper Cup final - Durutalo
item.description: The team that maintains discipline, minimises penalties and stays composed will have a better chance of lifting the Skipper Cup title, according to Fiji Rugby Union Head of Men’s High Performance Adriu Durutalo. In an exclusive interview with fijivillage Sports, Durutalo highlighted that discipline will be a key factor when Nadi takes on Nadroga in the Skipper Cup final at Churchill Park in Lautok
item.content:encoded:
The team that maintains discipline, minimises penalties and stays composed will have a better chance of lifting the Skipper Cup title, according to Fiji Rugby Union Head of Men’s High Performance Adriu Durutalo.

In an exclusive interview with fijivillage Sports, Durutalo highlighted that discipline will be a key factor when Nadi takes on Nadroga in the Skipper Cup final at Churchill Park in Lautoka today.

He says the competition has recorded a relatively high number of penalties per match, making discipline crucial for both teams.

Durutalo says whichever side settles into the match and minimises penalties will put itself in a stronger position to win.

The former USA Eagles Sevens player says Fiji has the potential to become the most disciplined team in world rugby if players remain direct and committed in their approach to the game.

Now settled into his new role as Head of Men’s High Performance, Durutalo says he is confident local players are ready for national selection if given the opportunity.

He says the Skipper Cup has reached the business end of the season, and he is impressed with the results players are achieving through their training and preparation.

Durutalo expects today's final to showcase running rugby, with both teams capable of moving the ball at pace for the full 80 minutes.

Nadi will face Nadroga in the final at 3pm today at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

item.title: Cold mornings no match for young swimmer Thaddeus Kwong's determination
item.description: Waking up early and getting into a cold swimming pool has been one of the biggest challenges for 17-year-old Thaddeus Kwong, as he prepares to represent Fiji at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal. However, the young swimmer says his determination and the support of his family continue to motivate him as he prepares to compete on the international stage.
item.content:encoded:
Waking up early and getting into a cold swimming pool has been one of the biggest challenges for 17-year-old Thaddeus Kwong, as he prepares to represent Fiji at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal.

However, the young swimmer says his determination and the support of his family continue to motivate him as he prepares to compete on the international stage.

Kwong, who is from Bucalevu and has maternal links to Motusa in Rotuma, says he is both nervous and excited about representing Fiji at the Games.

He says preparations have been going well, with his training now entering its final week of reduced intensity ahead of the competition.

Kwong says waking up early for training has not always been easy, particularly on cold mornings when getting into the pool requires extra motivation.

However, he says the encouragement and support he receives from his family help him push through those challenges.

The 17-year-old has already gained international experience, having represented Fiji at the Pacific Mini Games in Palau last year.

Kwong is also encouraging other young people to work hard, give their best and have faith in God as they pursue their dreams.

He thanks his parents, friends and family in Australia for their continued encouragement and support.

The Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, begins today and will run until 13th November.
